subject: Request: sub-50ms commitment for high-frequency inference (QuantaSense)
messages:

Subject: Request: sub-50ms commitment for our inference path

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. QuantaSense is excited about the latency profile we saw on the beta model, but our product team has a hard requirement: peak requests (inference + tokenization) must be under 50ms P95 for the real-time scoring endpoint. That requirement is tied to a customer pilot that starts next quarter.

Can Redwood provide a formal exception/commitment or a documented operational plan that guarantees sub-50ms P95 for a scoped traffic profile (<= 200 qps, histograms attached)? If this needs product work or a dedicated route, we need to understand timeline and any constraints before we proceed with the pilot.

Victor
VP Product, QuantaSense

Attachment: latency-sample-run.csv (csv, 120KB)

Agree this is priority. Initial assessment:
- Product perspective: sub-50ms P95 is aggressive but constrained scope (single model family, fixed prompt shape, bounded QPS) makes it plausible.
- Roadmap asks likely: pinned model variant, dedicated route with high-priority scheduling, and tighter batching/cold-start mitigations. We may need a short-lived runtime flag to force minimal batching for this customer's route.
- UX/observability: add per-route latency SLO dashboard to show P95 by window for contract compliance.

ETA: I can draft a feature/roadmap ask and a minimal runbook by 2026-10-25. Need Marcus to confirm if runtime flags + dedicated route are sufficient or if kernel-level work is required.

Lauren Bishop
Group PM, Redwood Console
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-20T13:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: sub-50ms commitment for our inference path

Quick infra check:
- Under the scoped profile (<=200 qps, short sequences) we can reach sub-50ms P95 if we provide:
  * Dedicated route (no noisy neighbors), pinned to an NVLink-connected GPU instance class we tested in June.
  * Forced minimal batching (max batch size = 4) for that route and pre-heated KV cache for common prefixes.
  * Model quantization to int8 and a tuned kernel path — this is already in our experimental kernels but not default for hosted customers.
- Risk: tail latency under unexpected bursts (spiky bursts > 200 qps) — mitigation is autoscaling + overflow policy to fallback model (slower but available).
- Ops impact: need a dedicated pool and an SRE runbook for prewarming; estimated infra delta ~$12k/mo at target utilization; dev effort ~3 engineer-weeks to expose the runtime flag properly and validate.

I’ll run a targeted perf test against QuantaSense sample (latency-sample-run.csv) and post results by 2026-10-22. If results look good, we can draft a formal amendment for the commitment.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Victor Chen <victor.chen@quantasense.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: sub-50ms commitment for our inference path — perf results

All — testing complete (summary):
- Test harness: replayed QuantaSense sample traces on pinned instance class with int8 quantization and KV prewarm.
- Results: P50 = 21ms, P95 = 46ms, P99 = 88ms (spikes linked to artificial I/O contention in one run). Median very healthy; P95 meets sub-50ms target under the test profile.
- Notes: Achieved numbers require the dedicated route + forced minimal batching + prewarm. Without dedicated pool, P95 rises to ~95ms under identical loads due to noisy neighbors.

Recommendation:
- We can offer a scoped SLA amendment that guarantees sub-50ms P95 for defined traffic shape and operational constraints (max sustained 200 qps, 15% burst headroom to 230 qps with autoscale/overflow to fallback).
- Operational asks: QuantaSense must provide a single model variant for the pilot and a daily warmup window (10 minutes) prior to business hours. SRE will run the prewarm.
- Commercial: estimated infra delta ~$12k/mo; include as a line item in amendment.

Next step: Hannah/Aditya — confirm commercial acceptance and finalize amendment. Lauren — incorporate these constraints into the runbook and add per-route SLO dashboards. I’ll attach raw perf CSV to the Drive link.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: latency-sample-run.csv (results appended to Drive)
